title: Head Trauma
markdown:
# Head Trauma

15 L/min O2 for all head trauma patients
Monitor O2, BP, HR every 3-5 min

### Airway/Breathing
O2 Sat less than 90%/or hypoventilation (despite non-rebreather)?
* **YES**: Basic airway measures \* -> Continue monitoring O2 sat and airway every 3-5 min
* **NO**: Continue monitoring O2 sat and airway every 3-5 min

#### REEVALUATE
O2 Sat less than 90% despite basic airway measures?
* **NO**: Continue monitoring O2 sat and airway every 3-5 min
* **YES**:
    * See Airway Algorithm - **Blue 2**
    * Avoid even MILD hyperventilation by using **Ventilation Rate Timer** and **Pressure-Controlled BVM, if available**
    * Carefully maintain goal ventilatory rates\*
    * Target EtCO2 to 40 mmHg (range 35-45 mmHg)

### Circulation
Hypotension \*\* or Other Signs of Shock?
* **NO**: Continue monitoring BP/HR every 3-5 min. Evaluate for early signs of shock.
* **YES**: IV fluid bolus. Repeat IV fluid bolus until hypotension resolves. -> Continue monitoring BP/HR every 3-5 min. Evaluate for early signs of shock.

### Disability
Document initial mental status, GCS **AND** any changes in mental status

> \* **Goal Ventilation Rates:**
> * **Age 0-2 years**: 1 breath every 2-3 seconds (25 BPM)
> * **Age 3-14 years**: 1 breath every 3 seconds (20 BPM)
> * **Age 15 years +**: 1 breath every 6 seconds (10 BPM)

> \*\* **Identifying Hypotension in Children:**
> * **Newborn**: 60 mmHg
> * **Age 0-2 years**: 70 mmHg
> * **Age 3-9**: 70+ (age x 2)
> * **Age 10 years or greater**: greater than 90 mmHg
>
> **General Rules:**
> * **Newborn**: greater than 60 mmHg
> * **5 Year Old**: greater than 80 mmHg
> * **10 years or greater**: greater than 90 mmHg
